Middle layer (Agent workspace): each Agent has a capability triangle — Tool (executable tools) / Skill (domain skills) / Knowledge (knowledge assets); internal Agents (Orchestrator/Executor/Environment/Report/Ticket) are maintained by the platform, external Agents (Diagnosis/Product) are independently deployed by partners/product teams. Lower layer (infrastructure): tool layer / monitoring and alerting / collaboration ticketing / knowledge platform (vectorization → MCP semantic retrieval) / AI capabilities (Qwen main model + OpenAI/Anthropic dual protocol) / data storage (Redis).
1bzn2t3:236: This article covers AI Native chaos engineering practice in Alibaba's private cloud IaaS scenarios: traditional chaos tools (Chaos Mesh/ChaosBlade/Gremlin) stay at the "inject and recover" stage; post-injection observability, diagnosis, and reporting rely on manual effort, preventing resilience verification from becoming high-frequency and routine. The Qwen solution uses a 9-layer Agent legion (Commander/Sentinel/Orchestrator/Executor/Environment/Diagnosis/Report/Ticket/Product) decoupled via a Redis shared blackboard, combined with three security gates and dual evolution loops, compressing a single verification loop from days to 40+ minutes and reducing manpower from dedicated SREs to 0.1 person per execution.
1d718ui:181: Three major pain points of traditional chaos engineering: high upfront test case design cost (manually designed fixed scenarios / real faults with multi-scenario combinations impossible to exhaust / each product line works in silos); mid-stage execution and diagnosis depend on manual work (untimely data collection / diagnosis based on experience / difficult recovery coordination); late-stage analysis is missing and results are hard to reuse (no complete injection analysis / hard to form standardized playbooks / hacks cannot be accumulated). Deep consequence: resilience verification can only be a periodic dedicated drill, unable to run frequently and routinely — real risk surfaces as production incidents in the gaps between drills.
